Four state governors on Saturday attended the grand finale of the ninth edition of the Festival of Champions, an outdoor outreach programme organised by the Redeemed Christian Church of God. The governors were Sheriff Oborevwori (Delta), Douye Diri (Bayelsa), Biodun Oyebanji (Ekiti) and Monday Okpebholo (Edo). The event, held at the Sports Field of Urhobo College, Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State, featured an all-night prayer and praise session that lasted into the early hours of Saturday. Other prominent attendees included the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele; the Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly and Chairman of the Conference of Speakers of State Legislatures of Nigeria, Emomotimi Guwor; the Ovie of Agbarha-Warri Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, Kingsley Orereh Igbi II; and Esther Tonlagha, wife of Niger Delta industrialist, Matthew Tonlagha. The General Overseer of the RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, who led the prayer sessions, urged worshippers to put their confidence in God, predicting miraculous breakthroughs for many before the end of the year. I will encourage you, therefore, if you believe, that before we enter the New Year, every obstacle before you would have vanished.” He added, “I have good news for someone here tonight. Before the end of the year, miracles are coming your way. You will laugh last over your misfortunes. Every evil force hindering your progress, you will never hear from them again. You will sing a new song. Just confess your sins and come to God.” The prayer and praise session featured performances by Nigerian and international gospel artistes, including Nathaniel Bassey, Muyiwa Olarewaju, Micah Stampley, Dunsin Oyekan, Mercy Chinwo, Chioma Jesus, Moses Bliss, Beejay Sax, Adeyinka Alaseyori, Lilian Nneji, Bidemi Olaoba, Bukola Bekes, Greatman Takit, Sounds of Salem, Tope Praise and South Africa’s Joyous Celebration. Speaking earlier, the Pastor-in-Charge of RCCG Champions Cathedral and Region 70, Pastor Emmanuel Emefienim, who convened the crusade, said the annual programme had grown in attendance, popularity and impact since its inception nine years ago. He described the Festival of Champions as an interdenominational outdoor outreach programme that brings Christians together to praise God, adding that the RCCG was privileged to host the event.
